tools.name: api_key_delete
tools.description: Delete an API key. Revokes the key at once. Requests that use it get 401 from then on.

tools.name: api_key_list
tools.description: List API keys. Your API keys. The secret itself is shown only once, when the key is created.

tools.name: api_key_rename
tools.description: Rename an API key

tools.name: chat_delete
tools.description: End an agent chat

tools.name: chat_list
tools.description: List agent chats

tools.name: chat_new
tools.description: Start an agent chat. Starts a chat in the VM. A VM keeps at most one empty chat: when it already has one, you get that.

tools.name: chat_send
tools.description: Send a message to an agent. Sends a prompt to a coding agent in the VM, in a new chat or the one named by `sessionId`. It answers at once; follow the chat in the dashboard or with the CLI.

tools.name: config_validate
tools.description: Validate a project config. Checks a `.homemade/config.json` or `.jsonc` file against the config schema. `.ts` and `.js` configs are checked at the first build instead.

tools.name: project_branches
tools.description: List branches. The branches a VM of this project can boot, the default branch first.

tools.name: project_create
tools.description: Create a project. Creates a project from a GitHub repository your team connected (`repo` as owner/name, or `githubInstallationId` + `githubRepoId`), from a starter (`template`), or empty. A new project starts its first VM on its own; `welcomeVm` says how that went.

tools.name: project_delete
tools.description: Delete a project. Deletes the project and every VM in it. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: project_get
tools.description: Get a project

tools.name: project_list
tools.description: List projects. Every project in your teams, newest first. Pass `orgId` for one team's projects.

tools.name: project_update
tools.description: Update project settings. Changes the project's slug, default branch, default auto-sleep and other settings. Every field is optional.

tools.name: sandbox_activity
tools.description: Get a sandbox's activity. What happened to the sandbox, oldest first: created, ready, every command and file write through the API, each extend. Commands are shortened, with the values of their env masked.

tools.name: sandbox_create
tools.description: Create a sandbox. Creates a sandbox: a throwaway VM with no project, on the plain base image or on one of your projects' images. It answers at once while the sandbox starts; a command sent to it waits until it is up. It never sleeps and is deleted when `ttlMinutes` runs out (default 60, at most 1440

tools.name: sandbox_delete
tools.description: Delete a sandbox. Deletes the sandbox and everything in it. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: sandbox_exec
tools.description: Run a command in a sandbox. Runs one command in the sandbox with `/bin/sh -lc` and answers its exit code and output. A sandbox that is still starting is waited for (up to a minute). The sandbox's own `env` is set, under the command's. Use `?stream=1` for commands that run longer than about 90 second

tools.name: sandbox_extend
tools.description: Extend a sandbox. Sets how long the sandbox lives from now: `ttlMinutes`, at most 1440 (24 hours).

tools.name: sandbox_get
tools.description: Get a sandbox. One sandbox: its state, size and when it is deleted.

tools.name: sandbox_list
tools.description: List sandboxes. Every sandbox in your teams that is not deleted, oldest first. With `ended=24h`, also the ones deleted in the last 24 hours, newest first.

tools.name: sandbox_read_file
tools.description: Read a file. Reads a file from the sandbox as text, or as base64 with `encoding=base64`. At most 10 MB.

tools.name: sandbox_write_file
tools.description: Write a file. Writes a file in the sandbox (text, or base64 for bytes), making its folders. Replaces a file already there. At most 10 MB.

tools.name: services_apply
tools.description: Apply services live. Changes the services of a running computer now, without updating the project: send the whole `.homemade/config.jsonc` text as `config` (or the `services` map). New and changed services start, removed ones stop, unchanged ones keep running, and their links follow. Only `services`

tools.name: services_health
tools.description: Get service health. Each service of a running computer: starting, healthy, failed (with its last log lines) or manual. With `waitSeconds`, waits until nothing is starting.

tools.name: setup_report
tools.description: Report setup progress. For coding agents running the setup at `/get-started.md`: tells the person's dashboard how far you got. Call it with `connected` right after signing in, `project` once the project exists, `checking` when Project Doctor starts, `done` with the pull request, or `failed` with a o

tools.name: shell_delete
tools.description: End a terminal session

tools.name: shell_list
tools.description: List terminal sessions. The VM's open terminals. Each one keeps running when nobody is attached.

tools.name: ssh_key_add
tools.description: Add an SSH key. Adds an SSH public key. Running VMs in your teams accept it within seconds.

tools.name: ssh_key_delete
tools.description: Remove an SSH key

tools.name: ssh_key_list
tools.description: List SSH keys

tools.name: vm_create
tools.description: Create a VM. Creates a VM from a project's latest build and starts it. The answer comes at once with the VM in `queued` or `booting`; poll `GET /api/vms/{vmId}` until `state` is `running`.

tools.name: vm_delete
tools.description: Delete a VM. Deletes the VM and its data. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: vm_dismiss_signal
tools.description: Dismiss the agent signal. Clears the attention signal an agent in the VM raised. Does nothing when there is none.

tools.name: vm_exec
tools.description: Run a command. Runs one command in a running VM as its user, with `/bin/sh -lc`, and answers its exit code and output. It opens no terminal. Use `?stream=1` for commands that run longer than about 90 seconds.

tools.name: vm_get
tools.description: Get a VM. The VM, its project, its services and its newest events. `vm.urls` holds each service's public URL by port.

tools.name: vm_list
tools.description: List VMs. Every VM in your teams that is not deleted, newest first. Pass `projectId` to list one project's VMs.

tools.name: vm_sleep
tools.description: Sleep a VM. Puts a running VM to sleep. It keeps its memory and disk and wakes where it left off. Sleeping an asleep VM answers 200.

tools.name: vm_update
tools.description: Update a VM. Renames the VM, changes its auto-sleep or who can open its services. Every field is optional.

tools.name: vm_wake
tools.description: Wake a VM. Wakes an asleep VM. Poll `GET /api/vms/{vmId}` until `state` is `running`.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Get the current user. The key's owner and the teams it can reach. A team's `id` is the `orgId` other calls take.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: chat_list, chat_new, setup_report, vm_get · Private data: api_key_delete, api_key_list, api_key_rename, config_validate, sandbox_activity, sandbox_read_file, sandbox_write_file, ssh_key_add, ssh_key_delete, ssh_key_list · Public sink: chat_send, services_apply · Destructive: api_key_delete, chat_delete, project_delete, sandbox_delete, sandbox_exec, shell_delete, ssh_key_delete, vm_delete, vm_exec.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: chat_list, chat_new, setup_report, vm_get · Private data: api_key_delete, api_key_list, api_key_rename, config_validate, sandbox_activity, sandbox_read_file, sandbox_write_file, ssh_key_add, ssh_key_delete, ssh_key_list · Public sink: chat_send, services_apply · Destructive: api_key_delete, chat_delete, project_delete, sandbox_delete, sandbox_exec, shell_delete, ssh_key_delete, vm_delete, vm_exec

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "sandbox_list" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "List sandboxes. Every sandbox in your teams that is not deleted, oldest first." → after: "List sandboxes. Every sandbox in your teams that is not deleted, oldest first. With `ended=24h`, also the ones deleted in the last 24 hours, newest first."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
